requirements.title: External files exist in a medium external to the program
requirements.definition: An external file is any file that exists in a medium external to the program.
requirements.oracle:
Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.

S12.3.1-001 I/O records/files runtime fixtures: scratch external files are connected to units and used for portable data transfer effects only; no medium implementation or storage representation is asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle.

S12.3.1-001 I/O records/files fixture boundaries: These fixtures are single-image positive runtime observations over internal CHARACTER files, scratch external files, and conservative local named files created in the execution working directory and deleted by the program. They assert only exact integers/logicals/characters, LEN before character equality, IOSTAT zero, and equality with the named IOSTAT_END constant. They do not assert byte sizes, record marker layout, IOMSG text, numeric IOSTAT values, ambient file existence, path syntax beyond the chosen local names, preconnected file identity, coarray image interactions, stream/record correspondence, or required diagnostics for mismatched forms/nonexistent files. Remaining facets stay pending with their source-accounting rationale.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11 for source form, names, expressions, execution constructs, and existing declaration/execution foundations. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: later clause 12 connection, specifier, file-position, data-transfer, internal-file, and input/output-item rules; clause 13 formatting; clause 15 defined I/O; clause 16 inquiry intrinsics where future fixtures need them; clauses 3, 5, 14, 17, 18, and 19 where terminology, constants, images, IEEE support, deleted features, or scope/lifetime controls are reached.

requirements.title: Allowed external-file access properties are processor dependent
requirements.definition: At any time, the sets of allowed access methods, forms, actions, and record lengths for a file are processor dependent.

pending.allowed-access-methods-processor-depende: No portable oracle may require a particular external file to allow sequential, direct, or stream access; future fixtures must choose processor-supported connections or guard support.
pending.allowed-forms-processor-dependent: No portable oracle may require all files to support both formatted and unformatted form.
pending.allowed-actions-processor-dependent: No portable oracle may require read, write, or readwrite action for every external medium.
pending.allowed-record-lengths-processor-depende: No portable oracle may assert a universal maximum or set of allowed record lengths.

requirements.definition: A file may have a name; a file that has a name is a named file; the name of a named file is represented by a character string value.

requirements.title: Same named file identity across images is processor dependent
requirements.definition: Whether a named file on one image is the same as a file with the same name on another image is processor dependent.

pending.same-name-cross-image-identity-processor: No single-image portable oracle exists, and even a multiimage profile must not require same-file or different-file identity solely from equal names.
